Poetic form: Rhymed couplet
Two successive verse lines share an end rhyme. A closed couplet also completes a grammatical unit.
Pattern: AA.

Poetic form: Tercet
A three-line stanza. Its lines may rhyme or remain unrhymed; the line count alone does not specify a complete rhyme scheme.

Poetic form: Quatrain
A stanza of four lines. Common arrangements include alternating rhymes and paired rhymes.
Possible patterns: ABAB or AABB.

Poetic form: Blank verse
Use a regular meter without end rhyme. English blank verse most often uses iambic pentameter: five broadly unstressed–stressed feet per line, with rhythmic variation.

Poetic form: Free verse
Organize verse through chosen rhythms and line breaks without a fixed metrical scheme. The absence of a fixed meter does not require the absence of patterned sound.

Poetic form: Shakespearean sonnet
Fourteen lines, conventionally in iambic pentameter: three quatrains followed by a couplet.
Rhyme arrangement: ABAB CDCD EFEF GG.

Poetic form: Petrarchan sonnet
Fourteen lines divided into an octave and a sestet. The octave commonly uses ABBAABBA; sestet rhymes vary. A turn in the argument often occurs between them.

text:
Poetic form: Villanelle
Nineteen lines: five tercets, then a quatrain. The opening stanza's first and third lines recur as refrains, becoming the final two lines.
Pattern: A1 b A2 / a b A1 / a b A2 / a b A1 / a b A2 / a b A1 A2.

Poetic form: Sestina
Six stanzas of six lines recycle six end words, followed by a three-line envoi using all six.
End-word order: ABCDEF / FAEBDC / CFDABE / ECBFAD / DEACFB / BDFECA.

Poetic form: Terza rima
Link three-line stanzas so that the middle rhyme of one becomes the outer rhyme of the next.
Pattern: ABA BCB CDC DED ...

Poetic form: Acrostic
Let the initial letters of successive lines spell a name, word, or phrase. The vertical reading adds a second structure to the horizontal one.

Poetic form: Ballad stanza
A common English narrative stanza alternates four-beat and three-beat lines, with the second and fourth lines rhyming.
Typical rhyme arrangement: ABCB.
